visual_goal: Show six overlapping waves of the stays industry, each leaving a layer of systems that is still running beneath today's platforms.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration of six overlapping ocean-like waves rolling across the width of the image, each wave a slightly different shade of blue, teal, green or orange, overlapping its neighbors. Under each wave crest sits a short label with its years, in this exact order from left to right: 'Reservation systems' with '1960s–1990s'; 'Online agencies' with '1991–2005'; 'European agency' with '1996–2012'; 'Vacation rentals' with '1995–2016'; 'Metasearch' with '2005–2018'; 'Convergence' with '2020–2026'. Beneath the waves, a cross-section of the ground shows six thin stacked sediment layers in the same six colors, one deposited by each wave, all still present under the newest wave at the right.
alt: Six overlapping waves from reservation systems in the 1960s to convergence in 2020–2026, each depositing a sediment layer that remains under the newest wave.

visual_goal: Contrast the OTA, which sells from a copy of the property's truth, with the hosted-stays marketplace, which owns the calendar it sells from but receives iCal copies hours late.
prompt: A two-lane illustration. Upper lane in a soft blue panel labeled 'Accommodation marketplace': left to right, a plain building with a small server labeled 'Hotel PMS', one arrow labeled 'ARI push' to a box 'Channel manager', one arrow to a gate box 'Gateway', one arrow to a cache box with a lightning icon 'Price cache', one arrow to a box 'Checkout'. One curved arrow from 'Checkout' back to 'Gateway', labeled 'reservation'. Lower lane in a soft teal panel labeled 'Hosted-stays marketplace': a phone icon labeled 'Host app' with one arrow labeled 'edits' into a large calendar page 'Platform calendar' in the middle of the lane; one arrow from the calendar to a box 'Checkout' on the right and one curved arrow from 'Checkout' back into the calendar. Below the calendar, a cluster of plain generic boxes labeled 'Other platforms' with one dashed arrow up into the calendar, beside a small clock icon, labeled 'hours late'.
alt: Upper lane: hotel PMS pushing ARI through a channel manager and gateway into a price cache and checkout, with reservations returning to the gateway. Lower lane: a host app editing the platform calendar that checkout reads and writes, with other platforms feeding it hours late.

visual_goal: Show the reference layering for a two-type group: shared guest channels, offer and reservation contract and platforms; one supply engine and connectivity edge per type.
prompt: A top-to-bottom layered illustration. Top: a wide band of small device icons labeled 'Guest channels', with one arrow down to a single green hub labeled 'Offer and reservation contract'. From the hub, three arrows go down: one to the left into a blue block labeled 'OTA supply engine', one in the middle into a wide orange block labeled 'Shared platforms', and one to the right into a teal block labeled 'Hosted-stays engine'. Under the blue block, one arrow down to a small blue plug-shaped block labeled 'Connectivity gateway'. Under the teal block, one arrow down to a small teal block with a phone icon labeled 'Host app and iCal'. The middle orange block has nothing below it.
alt: Guest channels feeding one offer and reservation contract, which sits above shared platforms and two separate supply engines, each with its own connectivity edge.
